name_structures.description: A Kinyarwanda name chosen for each child, plus a given name (often a Christian name in French or English form). The Kinyarwanda name is not inherited: most Rwandans do not share a family name with their parents or siblings
name_structures.source: Human Rights Watch, Leave None to Tell the Story, 1999, 'Language, Spelling and Names' (https://www.hrw.org/reports/1999/rwanda/Geno1-3-08.htm); Wikipedia, Rwandan names (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rwandan_names), accessed 5 Nov 2026

name_structures.description: Some accounts describe an optional third name from the father's side, or siblings' names sharing a root; others say surnames are not inherited. Unresolved: the benchmark models it as the varied parameter q (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.2)
name_structures.source: The New Times, 'Rwanda's Naming Traditions Explained', 6 May 2026 (https://allafrica.com/stories/202605070011.html), against HRW 1999 (above); RESEARCH_LOG.md, 26 Oct 2026

name_structures.description: A child may share one name element with a parent, but never all of them
name_structures.source: Rwanda, Law No 71/2024 governing persons and family, arts 38-39 (https://www.minijust.gov.rw/fileadmin/user_upload/Minijust/Publications/Laws/OG_n___Special_of_30.07.2024_Abantu_n_umuryango.pdf), as summarised in BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.2 [B1]; article text to re-read before release

order_rules.description: The national ID card has one field, Amazina ('names'), with no first/last split; the Kinyarwanda name is commonly written first, then the given name
order_rules.source: Wikipedia, Rwandan names, 'Official records', citing Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada, 'Rwanda: Procedures for obtaining the National Identity Card', 14 Oct 2010

order_rules.description: In Kinyarwanda and French publications the Kinyarwanda name comes first, often in capitals: MUGISHA Jean
order_rules.source: Africana Librarians Council (ALCASA), Africana Cataloging Guidelines, '4c. Name Order', via Wikipedia, Rwandan names

order_rules.description: In speech people are usually addressed by the given name; the Kinyarwanda name is used where a formal or identifying form is needed. A name reported orally may therefore be the given name alone
order_rules.source: Wikipedia, Rwandan names, 'Address in spoken life'

particles_and_morphemes.description: Name-initial elements described as feminine. Used ONLY to keep generated names consistent with generated sex; never to infer anyone's sex (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md C12)
particles_and_morphemes.source: Kimenyi, A. (1978), 'Aspects of Naming in Kinyarwanda', Anthropological Linguistics 20(6): 258-271 (https://www.jstor.org/stable/30027411); RESEARCH_LOG.md, 26 Oct 2026

particles_and_morphemes.description: Name-initial elements described as masculine. Same restriction: generation only, never inference

transliteration_rules.description: Ministerial order on Kinyarwanda orthography, gazetted Oct 2014, with two years to comply; it met public pushback, so old and new spellings coexist in records. The letter-level changes are NOT yet documented here: no rule is applied until the order's text is read
transliteration_rules.source: The New Times, 29 Oct 2014 (https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/112825/News/how-new-orthography-will-simplify-kinyarwanda) and 17 Nov 2014 (https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/113403); Niyomugabo & Uwizeyimana (2017), Language Policy 17(3): 307-318, doi:10.1007/s10993-016-9427-x

phonetic_rules.description: [r] and [l] are one sound. Spelling uses r, except l in proper nouns that already used it and unintegrated loanwords (Kigali, Kamali). A name may be written with either letter
phonetic_rules.source: 'Phonological Aspects of Loanword Adaptation in Kinyarwanda', IJLRHSS 3(3) (http://www.ijlrhss.com/paper/volume-3-issue-3/3-HSS-598.pdf); Wikibooks, Kinyarwanda/Orthography

phonetic_rules.description: Vowel length and tone are not written in the official orthography; linguistic texts write long vowels doubled (aa) and tone with accents. Search forms fold both; the original form is kept (CONCEPT-IDEA.md §5.3)
phonetic_rules.source: Wikibooks, Kinyarwanda/Orthography; Kinyarwanda and Kirundi Comparative Grammar (Dunwoody Press, 2007), Table 28 (https://www.matana.de/kirundi_kinyarwanda.pdf)

phonetic_rules.description: Written glide clusters are pronounced with a stop: rw [ɾɡw], sw [skw], tw [tkw], bw [bɡ], mw [mŋ], by [bɟ], ry [ɾɟ], py [pc], ty [tc]. Spelling follows the letters, speech does not
phonetic_rules.source: Wikipedia, Kinyarwanda, phonology (Cw/Cy table), accessed 5 Nov 2026; FSI Kirundi Basic Course, pronunciation synopsis; Nassenstein, Modern Africa (RESEARCH_LOG.md, 28 Oct 2026)

phonetic_rules.description: After m, the letter p stands for an aspirated [h]: impamvu [imhamvu]

common_administrative_forms.description: Kinyarwanda name in capitals before the given name (MUGISHA Jean). Capitals mark which element is the Kinyarwanda name; case is kept in the source value and folded only in search forms
common_administrative_forms.source: Wikipedia, Rwandan names, 'Written order and capitalisation'

phoneme_inventory.note: one sound; its phonemic status is disputed (accepted by Overdulve, Kimenyi; not by Coupez, Jacob, Bizimana)
phoneme_inventory.source: Kinyarwanda and Kirundi Comparative Grammar (2007), Tables 25-26

phoneme_inventory.note: one sound; phonemic status disputed as for cy
single letter c is an affricate
one sound; not accepted by Bizimana (1998)
accepted as a phoneme only by Kimenyi (2001); usually part of prenasalised ng
each read as one unit, not letter by letter

spelling_conventions.source: Wikipedia, Swahili language, 'Consonants' and 'Orthography', accessed 5 Nov 2026

spelling_conventions.note: Swahili has no /ʒ/; its j is [dʒ], so a Swahili writer likely writes j for both
spelling_conventions.source: Wikipedia, Swahili language, 'Consonants' (no /ʒ/ in the inventory)

listener_confusions.note: one sound in Kinyarwanda; heard and written either way (Kigali / Kigari; KAKOLELE / KAKORERE in UN 1533 aliases)
listener_confusions.source: IJLRHSS 3(3); UN Security Council Consolidated List, 1533 entries (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md [B12])

listener_confusions.note: written rw is said [ɾɡw]; a writer who does not know the spelling may write rgw or rugw
listener_confusions.source: Wikipedia, Kinyarwanda (Cw table); FSI Kirundi Basic Course; Nassenstein (RESEARCH_LOG.md, 28 Oct 2026). Pronunciation is sourced; how listeners write it is not

listener_confusions.note: written mw is said [mŋ]; may be heard as m + ng or mg
cy and c are close, and linguists disagree whether they contrast; may be written one for the other
shy may be heard and written as sh
listener_confusions.source: Comparative Grammar (2007), Table 26 (shy not accepted by Bizimana)

listener_confusions.note: the nasal of a prenasalised stop may be dropped or added (mb/b, nd/d)
listener_confusions.source: No source yet; listed so the matcher can test it at low weight

relationship_implications.note: Different Kinyarwanda names are expected among parents, children and siblings, so disagreement is no evidence against kinship. Agreement may be coincidence (common names) or the optional father element; accounts conflict (structure-father-element)
relationship_implications.source: HRW 1999; Law 71/2024 arts 38-39; The New Times, 6 May 2026

known_failure_modes.description: Systems with first/last fields split the single Amazina field in either order; MUGISHA Jean may be stored with Mugisha as first or last name. Compare across both orders
The Christian given name changes form with the writer's language (Jean / John / Yohana); handled by the cross-pack given-name data (week 4)
Pre- and post-2014 spellings, and the official orthography not being followed, give several written forms of one name (Uwimana / Uwimanna)
Names written by a clerk who hears the spoken form follow the sounds, not the spelling (rw as rgw, r as l); see listener_confusions
The same name in Kirundi spelling (Habyarimana / Havyarimana: by → vy, cy → c, jy → j, shy → sh); the rules belong to the bi-kirundi pack
Inferring sex from feminine or masculine prefixes is forbidden; a match is never scored up or down on it

protected_or_sensitive_forms.description: Identity cards before 1994 carried an ethnic category, and it was used to kill. The pack holds no ethnic, clan or religious marker, and any such field in a source is dropped on read
protected_or_sensitive_forms.source: HRW 1999, Geno1-3-10; DATA_RULES.md DR-1.7; THREAT_MODEL.md T8

protected_or_sensitive_forms.description: Names adopted in exile are not variants and get no public edge; tracing across a name change goes through the protected-person route

benchmark_cases.source: Comparative Grammar (2007), Table 1; Forebears, Burundi surnames

benchmark_cases.expected: possible same name (written by ear; hypothesis-weighted)
